metas.name: Argentina - Roadlines
metas.note: • Road lines in Argentina are mainly dashed white, double yellow or a mix in between.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Australia - Roadlines
metas.note: • Australia uses almost exclusively white road lines, with a few rare exceptions in alpine regions such as Mount Kosciuszko and Mount Hotham.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• Outside lines in Australia sometimes feature rumble strips that look like small white stripes perpendicular to the road line.

--- NOTE:

  • Northern Territory roads very rarely have rumble strips.
  • In addition, you can find similar rumble strips in New Zealand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Belgium - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Belgium uses all white road lines, these can be continuous or broken.
  • Roads are often accompanied by bike lanes on both sides.

NOTE: Bikes and cycling lanes are most common in the Netherlands, but they can be often seen in Belgium as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Botswana - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Like the other countries in Southern Africa, outside road lines (if present) are yellow, while centre road lines are white.

--- NOTE:

  • Outside yellow road lines in arid environments also exist in Israel, Palestine, Jordan, and the UAE.
  • However, these countries all drive on the right side.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Brazil - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Brazil will usually feature double yellow middle lines, with white outer lines.
  • Roads can occasionally have a single dashed yellow line.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Bulgaria usually has thin roadlines.
  • This is particularly useful to tell Bulgaria apart from Romania, where roadlines are usually much thicker.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bulgaria.

metas.name: Cambodia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads have dashed or solid yellow middle road lines.
  • Outer road lines are somewhat rare, but when present, they are solid white.

NOTE: Thailand uses similar road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Canadian roads usually have single yellow centre lines.
  • However, double middle yellow centre lines are still decently common.

NOTE: Double yellow centre lines are more common in the US. This is not a 100% reliable clue, so make sure to use this along with other clues.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Chile - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Chilean road lines are either all white or all yellow.
  • You will almost never see a combination of the two colours, apart from a few rare exceptions.

--- NOTE:

  • It is important to note that Argentina has a decent amount of roads with all white road lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Czechia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Czechia often has solid outer roadlines, with no centre line.

NOTE: While these roadlines can be found in all neighbouring countries, it is notably also common in Germany.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Denmark has all-white road lines. Double middle lines are very common.

NOTE: Some other European countries, most notably Poland and Greece, can have double middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• Outer road lines often consist of small white squares.
  • These unique-looking lines are a good way to identify Denmark.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Outer road lines sometimes consist of short dashes.

NOTE: Lithuania also sometimes has short dashes. In addition, Sweden primarily uses short dashes as outer road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Eswatini typically uses yellow outside lines and occasionally, triple white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar road lines can also be found in South Africa, Lesotho and Botswana.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Finland - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Where present, outer road lines will always be solid white lines.

NOTE: Unlike Sweden and Norway, Finland does not use dashed outside lines. The only exception to this are the Åland Islands in southwest Finland, which do use dashes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: France - Roadlines
metas.note: • Typical French roads have long spaced out dashes on the outside.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• These middle road lines, where each dash consists of two offset blocks, are unique to France.
  • They are not extremely common, but when you see them, you can safely guess France.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Roadlines #3
metas.note:
• Middle lines with dashes that are longer than usual can be a good clue for France.

NOTE: Unusually long dashes are also common in the UK.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Road lines in Ghana are always white.
  • However, many paved roads do not have road lines at all.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Greece - Roadlines
metas.note:
• In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines.
  • This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Roadlines #2
metas.note: • Yellow road lines are more common in Greece than any other southern European country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Guatemala - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Similarly to Mexico, Guatemalan roads generally have solid white outer lines with a single yellow middle line.
  • Road lines in Guatemala are generally significantly thinner than in Mexico.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guatemala for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Roadlines / Bicycle lanes
metas.note: • While Hungarian road lines are all-white, lines on bicycle lanes are typically yellow.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Indonesia uses white or yellow centre lines.
  • Outer lines will always be white. The centre lines will be solid or dashed.

NOTE: Malaysian road lines are always all white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Roadlines
metas.note:
• It is very common to see yellow outside dashes on Irish roads.

NOTE: This is essentially never found in the UK. These dashes can also be seen in New Zealand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Israel - Roadlines
metas.note: • Most roads feature yellow outer lines with white centre lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Roadlines
metas.note:
• One of the most common types of Italian road lines are white solid outer lines with no middle line.
  • This is generally less common in other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Roadlines
metas.note:
Japan has three common variations of road lines. They are as follows:

  • The most common being white, solid outer lines with a dashed white middle line.
  • White solid sidelines with a yellow solid middle line.
  • White solid sidelines with yellow and white middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Jordan typically feature yellow outside and white middle lines.

NOTE: Other Middle Eastern countries such as the UAE and Israel can also have these road lines. Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Roadlines
metas.note: • Outer lines in Kenya will always be solid white, while inner lines will be yellow and either solid or dashed.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Lesotho - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Lesotho uses yellow outer lines and white inner lines.

--- NOTE:

  • These are also found in the other three southern African countries.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• Some roads have unique triple middle lines, consisting of two solid lines with a dashed line in between.

--- NOTE:

  • These are also found in the other three southern African countries, but nowhere else in the world.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Malaysia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Malaysia frequently uses double white centre lines on its two-lane roads.
  • It is the only Southeast Asian country to do so.
  • Middle lines can also be dashed on one-lane roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The most typical Mexican road lines are white solid outer lines with a single unbroken yellow middle line.

NOTE: Single broken yellow middle lines and double yellow middle lines are also common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Like most of Europe, the Netherlands has all-white road lines.
  • Many roads have dashed outside lines.
  • Sometimes, you can find unique green middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• Like most of Europe, the Netherlands has all-white road lines.
  • Many roads have dashed outside lines.
  • Sometimes, you can find unique green middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Roadlines
metas.note:
• New Zealand normally uses white outer road lines.
  • Yellow dashed outer road lines can be seen in populated areas.
  • Roads with no outer lines can be seen on smaller roads.
  • Inner lines are either a single dashed white line or unbroken double yellow lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Australia does not have yellow inside lines, apart from regions with snow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Norway - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Smaller Norwegian roads typically have long dashed white outer lines, while larger roads have solid outer lines and yellow middle lines.
  • The yellow lines have a distinct tinge of orange.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Roadlines #2
metas.note: • Road lines will often be made up of small dots of paint.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Oman use yellow outer and white middle lines.

NOTE: This is also common in the UAE, Israel, Jordan, as well as occasionally found in Qatar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Panama - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Panama features a diverse set of road lines, but the most common combination is solid outer white with an inner yellow line. However, those are not unique to Panama.
  • Within Latin America, solid outer white lines with no middle line are almost unique to Panama.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/panama for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Peruvian roads always have white outer lines.
  • On highways, you will find either single yellow dashed or double yellow middle lines.
  • On rural mountain roads, you will most likely see white outer lines without any centre line.

--- NOTE:

  • In the continent of South America, rural mountain roads, with the features mentioned above, are predominantly found in Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Philippines - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Middle road lines in the Philippines can be either yellow or white, they can also be full white.
  • In particular, you will often see combined yellow and white middle lines, which is not common in any other East Asian country.
  • Yellow road lines commonly have a distinct orange tint.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Poland has all-white road lines.
  • Double middle lines are very common and usually a good clue for Poland.

NOTE: Some other European countries, most notably Denmark and Greece, can have double middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Qatar typically uses solid outer white lines with either white or yellow in the middle.
  • More rarely, you can also find outer yellow lines too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Middle lines are often noticeably thicker than average.
  • This is especially useful to tell Romania apart from Bulgaria, which generally has thinner road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Roadlines
metas.note: • Being a former French colony, Senegal uses French infrastructure such as bollards, poles, signs and road lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Singapore - Roadlines
metas.note: • Main roads are often divided, and commonly feature black-and-white curbs and double yellow outside lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Slovenian roads commonly feature long outer dashes.

NOTE: Neighbouring countries do not frequently use dashed outside lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Roadlines
metas.note:
• On most roads, South Africa utilizes single yellow outer lines and white centre lines.

--- NOTE:

  • The other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, and Lesotho also use single yellow outer lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• South Africa occasionally features unique white triple centre lines with 2 solid lines on the outside and a dashed line on the inside.
  • You may also sometimes encounter another unique triple centre line, consisting of two white lines with one yellow line in the middle.
  • These centre lines are usually found on larger main roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Korea - Roadlines
metas.note: • Roads have yellow middle lines and white outer lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Rural roads often have outside lines, but no middle lines.
  • In the absence of other clues, this can sometimes be a way to decide a tough 50-50.

NOTE: Most small roads lack road lines entirely.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Roadlines
metas.note:
• On smaller roads, the outer road lines are white and dashed.
  • They are distinctly shorter than the Norwegian dashed lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• The outer road lines on highways look solid from a distance, but are typically divided into small sections with a unique pattern, which is different from the solid lines in Finland and Norway.
  • Road lines in Denmark can have a similar pattern, however the individual sections should be rectangular.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Taiwan generally feature double yellow middle lines with single white outer lines.
  • Thinner roads sometimes use single dashed yellow lines instead.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• Roads with outside white road lines and no middle lines at all are common.
  • In the absence of better clues, this type of road line can be a very good way to identify Taiwan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Thailand has yellow middle lines. These middle lines are either solid or dashed lines.

NOTE: Malaysia only has white middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Tunisia usually has white road lines.
  • Outer road lines can be dashed or solid.

--- NOTE:

  • A few roads in Sfax have yellow middle lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Turkey - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent.
  • Most roads simply have white road lines. However, it is not uncommon to see yellow road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Outer roadlines are yellow, middle lines are white.
  • They can also be full yellow.

NOTE: Other Middle Eastern countries, like Jordan, Israel and Oman, also use these lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Double yellow road lines are often found on the sides of marked roads, especially in urban areas.
  • These lines indicate a no stopping zone.

NOTE: These lines can also be found in Ireland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United States of America - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The US uses yellow middle lines and white outer lines.
  • Double middle lines are the most common.
  • On divided roads, the outer line closest to the median will be yellow, and the other lines will usually be white.

--- NOTE:

  • Double middle lines are less common in Canada, but not rare – use this meta with caution.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america.

metas.name: United States of America - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• Interstate highways, US highways, and some state roads have rumble strips in each edge of the road; which are small indentations in the pavement perpendicular to the road.

--- NOTE:

  • Rumble strips may appear in Canada, but are much more rare.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america.

metas.name: Uruguay - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Uruguay often has these triple road lines, that consist of double yellow roadlines with white dashes in between.
  • This is a design not seen anywhere else in the Americas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uruguay for more clues.

metas.name: Uruguay - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
You can also find two other, non-unique road line patterns:

  • Yellow-white lines (also found in Argentina)
  • Simple white lines (found in many other places).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uruguay for more clues.
